content:
I had an LLM audit mathlib for malformed citation syntax after noticing a few broken links in the docs. It turned up with various types of issues, which I've PR'd separately:

  • #44668: Fixing newline breaks in [text][key] citations (resulted in broken links),
  • #44669: Change relative links [text](key) to proper citation links [text][key], merged
  • #44671: A trivial typo with a 5 year old history, merged
  • #44673: Add citation keys to free-text citations, merged
  • #44758: fix references.bib keys whose year does not match the entry, merged
  • #44674: Fix typos in citation keys that resulted in broken links.

Another issue is that we sometimes have free-text citations to works that aren't present in the references.bib file yet, e.g. here. I will work on finding all of these and adding them to our references, but that needs a bit more review than these mechanical fixes.

I guess you probably have a backlog of things to do somewhere (like I do), but just in case you missed them, seems like there are also few citations with missing bib entries: casteran, janusz1996, knuth1997, russell1974, and schneider2013.
Yes, they've been found by LLM as well and I will add them!

Also, we currently have a wild mix of competing conventions when naming keys in references.bib:

Convention Examples Count
lowercase author + year rudin1991, aluffi2016 205
no year / descriptive atiyah-macdonald, borceux-vol1, Elephant 61
Capitalized author + year Stone1938, Geck2017 49
underscores abramsky_gabbay_maibaum_1994, Adamek_Rosicky_1994 43
hyphens cartan-eilenberg-1956, Roby-1963 40
Google Scholar style cassels1967algebraic, rudin2006real 40
2-digit year har77, hatcher02 22
CamelCase RiehlVerity2022, EinsiedlerWard2017 20
MathSciNet ID MR0236876, MR399081 18
other boydVandenberghe2004, CARBONI1993145 12

I think this creates confusion. Should we pick a standard and enforce it in lint-bib.sh?
I think the convention there is "paste the name from whatever tool that generated the bib blob for you" :smile:
I think we can do better! Given that Justus is already fixing citations, why don't we choose a convention and stick to it?

Weiyi Wang said:

I think the convention there is "paste the name from whatever tool that generated the bib blob for you" :smile:

Yes, but it creates confusion when adding citations (see #44674). Apparently bibtool, which is called by lint-bib.sh, can generate keys from a format string (key.generation=on with key.format=…). We currently don't enable that, so it only sorts and formats the entries.
Could you also check that if there are duplicated bibliography entries? Since the same article can potentially added twice with different naming keys (due to different naming convention).

David Ang said:

I think we can do better! Given that Justus is already fixing citations, why don't we choose a convention and stick to it?

This would cause extra noise (because the community would not know the convention so would continually have to be corrected) and the issue is completely minor (certainly my personal bibtex file has many conventions, because there are many competing conventions in the wild and I don't care to normalise). Is it worth the effort?

I guess the usual response to ideas like this is "if we do choose a convention and make a churny PR fixing it then it should come with a linter enforcing the convention, or else in 6 months' time we're back to square 1 and it was all a waste of time". So ultimately the outcome is either "mathlib is slower" or "we have to continually make PRs enforcing the convention" and this sounds like an argument against having a convention.

Yes, but won't the upcoming Verso docstrings overhaul this anyways? I don't know a lot about this or the plans, but I'd guess that a "role" will be assigned to references, and maybe citation syntax will become something like [cite]`foo bar baz`​?
Okay I now agree that it's better to wait for Verso than to enforce a standard for key names now.

The PRs above are ready for review again and I concluded this audit by making two more, which add new entries to our references:

  • #44767: add missing bib entries for keys merged. These are the ones mentioned by @David Ang above,
  • #44773: add missing bib entries for free-text citations. This one adds 22 entries to references.bib that were previously mentioned only in free-text.
It seems that the new Verso syntax will be {cite "key"}[text]
